Skipped the optional full end-to-end regeneration timing test (~90s) since backend book creation & burn accounting was already exhaustively verified via curl this iteration per the review request context.
critical_code_review_comments: pricing.py is cleanly separated as pure config (no DB/auth imports) — good. TIERS/WRITER_STYLES/STORE_ITEMS/REFILL_PACKS use consistent dict-of-dicts shape and helpers (allowed_styles_for_tier, style_multiplier, estimate_word_cost) keep the math out of routers.
deps.py extraction of get_current_user to break auth.py↔credits.py circular import is correct and minimal.

credits.adjust_balance uses find_one_and_update with $inc + a separate credit_transactions insert — this is NOT atomic (a crash between them yields drift). Non-critical for MVP but worth noting; would need a Mongo transaction or an idempotency key for real-money-adjacent ledger integrity once $NEUR is real.

payments._finalize_paid_transaction relies on caller's payment_status transition (guarded by update_one with $ne:paid) to enforce exactly-once — correct pattern for both the status-poll and webhook paths.

books.create_book computes estimated_cost but the actual burn happens later in generation.run_generation per chapter — this means a user can start a book at ~exactly balance boundary and end up with slight overspend if actual generated word count exceeds estimate*multiplier. Consider reserving the estimated_cost up front (or capping generation to estimate) for robustness. Non-blocking for MVP.
auth.register grants stipend inline (writes credit_balance + creates ledger row) but does NOT call ensure_monthly_stipend afterwards — correct, since last_stipend_at is set to now(). Clean.
InsufficientCreditsModal replaced UpgradeModal cleanly; store link points to /store with a clear CTA. Good UX for the new economy.

One minor visual note only (not fixed): The Clockwork Requiem card on Laureate's dashboard shows 'cover locked' because illustrations_unlocked defaults False for pre-existing older books. Not a bug per new schema, but the migration story for older books is worth confirming with the product owner (should legacy premium-generated books auto-set illustrations_unlocked=true?).
